standardized annual shoot length (a proxy for tree-ring growth) of alpine Pinus pumilain central Japan increased during 1950-2009, and that this increase was mainly due to increasing temperature.

standardized indices of shoot length of Pinus pumilla in central Japan increased more than tree-ring width during 1951-2009, and that high temperatures at beginning of growing season increased both shoot length and tree- ring width.

the annual shoot length (a measure of tree growth rate) and tree-ring widths (a measure of growth rate) of alpine Pinus pumilaincreased during 1951-2009, that high temperatures in the beginning of the current growing season increase both annual shoot length and growth rates, and that analyzing the annual shoot length may overestimate the influence of temperature on growth rates.
